title: Flip (mirror) an axis, not just turn: e.g. X pointing left with Y to the back and Z up

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-08):

> In all of the manipulation we can do to the world/coordinate axes, we have turn x, y, z plus and minus.. but we don't have the "flip axis".. in some cases we need X pointing left and Z up.. but that makes Y point the wrong way and it needs to be "inverted".. I need X to point left and Y towards the back.. and I cannot achieve that by just turning the axes, it needs to be flipped / mirrored.

## Why turning can't do it
X left, Y back, Z up is the basis (-X, +Y, +Z): determinant -1, a **left-handed** frame. Every rotation (turn about X/Y/Z, the presets of #326/#341, the plane picks of #330) keeps handedness, so no combination of turns reaches it - only a reflection (mirror one axis) does. The part-alignment and work-offset code deliberately accepts rigid transforms only (#341 refuses a non-rigid transform in a file as corrupt), so this is a new capability, not a missing preset.

## Why this is safety-critical
Machine coordinate systems are right-handed by standard (ISO 841 / RS-274). A mirrored frame changes the meaning of the program: arc direction (G2 <-> G3), cutter-compensation side (G41 <-> G42), climb vs conventional milling, thread hand, and canned cycles that assume a direction. Getting this wrong cuts a mirror-image part or gouges. Any mirror support must be explicit, labelled, and either compensated consistently through generation, verification and post, or refused by name.

## Open questions (why needs-research)
Which of these is actually wanted - they are different features:
1. **View / display only** - see the part and axes as if standing at the back of the machine (axes triad and viewport flipped), with no change to geometry or the posted program. Lowest risk.
2. **Machine axis direction** - the machine's X+ physically moves the other way (or the operator stands at the back); a per-machine `.mch` setting whose post writes the axis with inverted sign, while the CAM side stays right-handed. Needs a per-post check for G2/G3, G41/G42 and arc-centre sign handling.
3. **Mirror the part** - machine the opposite-hand part (left/right versions of one design): reflect the geometry and regenerate, so toolpaths, arcs and comp sides are correct for the mirrored part (not a mirrored program).
4. **Controller mirror image** (G51.1 / mirror-image function): post a mirror command and let the control mirror - only where the dialect supports it, refused elsewhere.
Also decide: per setup (like #326 alignment) or per document; how it shows in the WCS (#342) and setup sheet; interaction with rotated-offset refusal (#315) and the axis-fit/rotary code.

## Proposed breakdown (after the questions are answered)
- [ ] Decide which of 1-4 (one or more) and record it
- [ ] Display flip (if wanted)
- [ ] Machine axis-direction setting + post sign handling + G2/G3/G41/G42 tests (if wanted)
- [ ] Part mirror as a new geometry operation with handedness-aware regeneration (if wanted)
- [ ] Refusals by name everywhere the mirror is not supported

Related: #326 (PR #341 part alignment), #330 (plane picks), #342 (one WCS per setup), #315 (rotated offsets refused), #308.
